records.text: The Republican National Committee changed its convention rules to bind delegates to state primary or caucus winners and refused to recognize Ron Paul's Maine delegates.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: my producer has a note that the RNC altered the convention rules to bind delegates in future elections to vote for the candidate who wins their state's primary caucus or caucus. ... The RNC also refused to recognize Paul's delegates from Maine.

verification.notes: Congressional Research Service and contemporaneous convention reporting document the 2012 Republican rule changes requiring delegate allocation consistent with statewide results and the credentials dispute that replaced ten of the twenty-four Maine delegates aligned with Ron Paul. The statement is a fair summary of those events.

records.text: Charlie Kirk said, “I'm going to probably take control of the RNC.”
records.speaker: Charlie Kirk

appearances.snippet: He kind of scrawled and scribbled, and wrote that his structure is currently a 501(c)(3), and he's sitting there talking to me: “But here's what we can do in the future, and here's how, and then I'm going to probably take control of the RNC.”

verification.notes: Unverifiable: This is Candace Owens recounting a private conversation with Charlie Kirk from many years earlier (when he was 23) where he allegedly discussed future plans to 'take control of the RNC'. While Kirk did become influential within Republican circles and his Turning Point USA partnered with the RNC in 2024, there is no way to verify what was said in this private conversation at a Macaroni Grill at Chicago O'Hare. Kirk did speak at the 2024 RNC and had close relationships with Trump campaign officials, but whether he specifically stated he would 'take control of the RNC' in this early conversation cannot be independently confirmed. Sources: Washington Post, National Memo, CBS News on Kirk's 2024 RNC involvement.

conveyance.original_source: Private conversation recounted by Candace Owens

records.text: Candace Owens said Charlie Kirk was 23 when he spoke to her about taking over the RNC.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: I mean, he's 23 years old, right? ... And he's talking, speaking to me about how he's going to... ... take over the RNC.

records.text: Candace Owens recalled that, at age 23, Charlie Kirk envisioned Turning Point USA becoming the world’s largest conservative student organization and discussed eventually taking control of the RNC
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: And what he had envisioned was for Turning Point USA to become the biggest conservative student organization—not just in the nation, by the way, but in the world. ... He kind of scrawled and scribbled, and wrote that his structure is currently a 501(c)(3), and he's sitting there talking to me: “But here's what we can do in the future, and here's how, and then I'm going to probably take control of the RNC.” ... I mean, he's 23 years old, right? ... And he's talking, speaking to me about how he's going to... ... take over the RNC.

verification.notes: Verified as a first-person attribution claim from Owens’s primary recording. She describes the O’Hare planning session, quotes Kirk’s global student-organization ambition and probable future control of the RNC, and immediately identifies him as 23. The statement preserves that private recollection as attributed testimony rather than claiming independent documentary proof of the menu notes.
